title: function-calling parse debug scratchpad (Maya)
content:
Quick scratchpad for the recurrent function-calling parsing failures we've been seeing in hosted-api (observed across multiple customers). Dumping notes, commands I ran, error snippets, hypotheses and next actions.

Summary of symptoms:
- Model returns something that looks like JSON but the parser throws a JSON.parse error in the runtime: e.g. 'Unexpected token A in JSON at position 0' or 'Unexpected end of JSON input'.
- Failures tend to happen when streaming responses + function call mode are enabled (~20% of requests).
- Some cases show the model returning explanatory text before or after the JSON payload (e.g. "Answer:" prefix or trailing "\n" characters).
- Other cases show unescaped newlines or Python-style single quotes instead of double quotes.

Repro steps I used locally:
1) Minimal curl to reproduce (hosted):
   curl -X POST "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat/completions" \\
     -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN' \\n     -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \\n     -d '{\"model\":\"rwd-3b-instruct\",\"messages\":[{\"role\":\"system\",\"content\":\"You are a JSON-only responder. Reply with ONLY the JSON for the function call.\"},{\"role\":\"user\",\"content\":\"Return a function call with name 'set_timer' and args {duration: 5}\"}],\"functions\":[{\"name\":\"set_timer\",\"parameters\":{\"type\":\"object\",\"properties\":{\"duration\":{\"type\":\"integer\"}},\"required\":[\"duration\"]}}],\"stream\":false}'

2) Observed body in runtime logs (raw):
   "Answer:\n   {\n     'name': 'set_timer',\n     'arguments': {duration: 5}\n   }\n\n   Note the single quotes and unquoted keys.

3) Re-ran with temperature=0 and a stricter system prompt. Outcome: reduced frequency, but still flaky when input contains multi-line user content.

Sample error snippets from runtime stderr / parser:
- "SyntaxError: Unexpected token A in JSON at position 0"
- "JSON.parse: unexpected character at line 1 column 1 of the JSON data"
- "Parsing function args failed - missing \"arguments\" field"
- Log excerpt (2024-10-28T14:23:11Z): Received payload chunk b'\\xef\\xbb\\xbf{\"name\":\"set_timer\"' -> parser rejected (BOM + streaming boundary)

Hypotheses:
- Model occasionally emits non-JSON prefixes/suffixes (e.g., "Answer:", explanatory text) which breaks strict JSON.parse.
- Streaming chunk boundaries can split JSON tokens across frames (e.g., opening brace in one chunk, remainder in next) and our reassembly code may be dropping/duplicating bytes when rejoining. BOM (UTF-8 BOM) seen once \u2014 need to strip BOMS earlier.
- The model sometimes returns Python-style dicts / single quotes when instruction-following is imperfect, especially for smaller instruction-tuned variants.
- When functions have nested objects, the model may omit quotes on keys (e.g., {duration: 5}) \u2014 the schema validator then errors out.
- Some proxies / client SDKs may be auto-prettifying or adding whitespace/newlines; our parser expects compact JSON and fails on trailing commas or comments (though comments are rare).

Commands/tricks tried:
- Enforced "You MUST reply with only valid JSON. No commentary." system prompt (helpful but not sufficient).
- Set temperature=0 and top_p=0.0 (fewer creativity errors). Frequency of issue dropped ~3x.
- Post-parse tolerant mode: replaced JSON.parse with a safer parser that attempts to fix single quotes -> double quotes, remove "Answer:" prefix, strip BOM, and wrap unquoted keys (quick heuristic). This parsed ~70% of malformed payloads in local tests, but feels brittle.
- Streaming reassembly: added a buffer that concatenates incoming chunks and only attempts parse when last chunk indicates end-of-message ("[DONE]" token). This eliminated some chunk-split issues but we still saw cases where model sends extra whitespace or newlines after JSON and before [DONE].
- Added a regex to remove leading non-json bytes: ^[^\{\[]+ -> strip, then attempt parse. Catches "Answer:" but may mask real problems.

Notes on schema vs model output:
- When function parameters contain nested objects or arrays, model mistakes are more frequent. Example failing model output for schema {\"type\":\"object\", \"properties\": {\"timer\":{\"type\":\"object\",\"properties\":{\"duration\":{\"type\":\"integer\"}}}}}: model emitted {\"name\":\"set_timer\", \"arguments\": \"{\\\"timer\\\": {\\\"duration\\\": 30}}\"} (arguments as string) -> runtime interpreted arguments as string instead of object.

Potential fixes (ordered by low->high effort):
1) Client-side resilient parser: keep current safe heuristics (strip BOM, remove non-json prefix, replace single->double quotes) but log and increment metric for heuristics applied. If heuristics triggered > X% -> alert.
2) Streaming reassembly improvement: ensure we track byte offsets and use a deterministic concat strategy; reject if chunk sizes inconsistent. Add tests that simulate chunk splits at every byte boundary.
3) Model-side mitigation: make function signature examples extremely explicit in system prompt and include "JSON only, must use double quotes, keys quoted, no surrounding text" plus a canonical example. Consider adding a short unit in the prompt showing expected output for small/complex nested args.
4) Fallback run: if parse fails, call the model again with the original conversation + "You MUST output only the JSON corresponding to the function call, fix the previous answer. Do not explain." and set temperature=0. This adds latency but increases success.
5) Add a fast sanity-check step: after parsing, run the parsed object against our JSON Schema (AJV) and reject if invalid. For strings that look like JSON but are actually strings, attempt JSON.parse on the field and validate. Log examples to S3 for triage.

Telemetry / metrics to add:
- count_parse_errors_total (per model, per deployment)
- parse_heuristic_applied_total (which heuristics)
- parse_retries_triggered_total and success_rate_on_retry
- avg_latency_of_first_parse vs retry_parse

Next steps / TODOs:
- [ ] Add unit tests for streaming reassembly that split a valid JSON at every position and reassemble. (Owner: Ashwin)
- [ ] Add opt-in tolerant parser behind feature flag and collect metrics for 1 week. (Owner: Maya)
- [ ] Update function-calling prompt templates with canonical examples for nested args and enforce double quotes. (Owner: Olivia)
- [ ] Add a Confluence page with examples of common broken outputs and our heuristics (link to Confluence in linked_artifacts). (Owner: Ethan)
- [ ] Small follow-up: run a sweep of logs for anything containing "Unexpected token" between 2024-10-01 and 2024-11-02 and sample 200 examples to S3. (Owner: Maya)

Notes / breadcrumbs from slack and infra:
- Slack thread: #eng-runtime reported similar errors on 2024-10-25 after a canary deploy. Possible correlation with runtime v1.12.4 -> v1.13.0 (PR 512 changed streaming buffer code).
- Infra log snippet: request_id=abc123 stream_recv 14:23:11: chunk sizes [512, 512, 120] -> last chunk contained only '}}\n' and we incorrectly trimmed leading whitespace.

Scrap / ideas that probably won't fly:
- Always force model responses through a secondary canonicalizer model to rewrite into JSON \u2014 adds cost and tail latency.
- Strictly reject any response that isn't parseable and return error to user (bad UX).

If we go the heuristics-first route, we should make heuristics explicit and measurable and add an automated sample uploader so ops/ML can inspect failed parses with full context (messages, model, params, raw chunks).

Raw examples to keep for triage bucket (copy exact payloads below):
- Example 1 (single-quote keys): '\n  {\n    'name': 'set_timer',\n    'arguments': {'duration': 5}\n  }'

- Example 2 (arguments as string): '\n  {\"name\":\"set_timer\", \"arguments\": \"{\\\"timer\\\": {\\\"duration\\\": 30}}\"}\n'

- Example 3 (prefix + BOM): '\n  \ufeffAnswer:\n  {\"name\":\"set_timer\",\"arguments\":{\"duration\":5}}\n

End of scratchpad. Will iterate as we get more logs.

Timestamped quick edits:
- 2024-11-03: added BOM observation and example.
- 2024-11-05: noted correlation with streaming buffer PR 512; assigned Ashwin for streaming unit tests.
